To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction between phospholambans and the Ca2+-ATPase of cardiac sarcoplastic reticulum (PLN and SERCA) is mediated by multiple sites of interaction that are located in the cytoplamic and transmembrane regions of both proteins.
both the cytoplasmatic and the transmembrane interaction domains in phospholamban and in the Ca2+ATPase of cardiac sarcopasmic reticulam are essential for normal function.

the sites of functional interaction between PLN and SERCa2 are located in both the cytoplasm and transmembrane domains and that the sites in both the cyto- and trans- domains are made up of both charged and hydro- phobic amino acid residues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which the Ca2+ pump is regulated by the protein phospholamban and by the protein phosphatase inhibitor protein 1 (I-1).
the identification of the amino acids involved in the functional interactions between PLN and SERC2.
the molecular basis of the regulation of the SERCA2 by PLN and with the molecular basis for the regulation of PLN by the phosphatases and protein kinases that are known to phosphorylate PLN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PLN and SERC2a interact through a complex and diffuse site of interaction.

the interaction site in SERCA2 consists of the linear sequence LDDKPV402 and that the interaction site on PLN is a complex, but highly specific site, which is located between the first 20 residues on the cytoplasmatic side and the transmembrane domain.
the interaction site between phospholambamn and SERCA2 is a complex of charged and hydrophophic residues in both cytoplasmic and transmembrane domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction between PLN and SERCAR2 occurs at two distinct sites, one on each protein.
the interaction site between SERCA2 and PLN is composed of two regions.
the interaction site in PLN and SERC2 is complex and involves multiple residues in the cytosolic domains of both proteins and possibly the transmembrane domain of PLN.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sites of functional interaction are not confined to a small number of specific amino acids, but rather are distributed along the length of the molecules and are made up of charged and hydrophic residues.
PLN and SERC2A interact in multiple ways.
the sites of functional interaction between SERCA2 and phospholambam are more complex than previously thought.
